applies_why: The judge text uses Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 to break C3's link and labels it 'CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN' without quoting or naming the earlier round that pressed those verses.
quote: CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way.
room: counted this way — whether it applies only to formal unanswered-witness counts or also to any verse used to break a link; I read it as also covering break-link verses.
why: Because K-G4 counts a verse used to break a link this way, the judge had to quote the earlier-round sentence pressing the verse against the link and name the round, but the text names no rounds and quotes no such sentence.
